newsitem.title: CHILE: SOCCER-RIOT POLICE SHIELD REFEREE FROM PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RIOT POLICE SHIELD REFEREE FROM PLAYERS.

text.p: Riot police intervened to stop a referee being attacked by furious Flamengo players after the Brazilian team were knocked out of the South American Supercup.
Flamengo lost 1-0 to Chile's Colo Colo in a bad-tempered game on Thursday during which three players were sent off.
At the end of the match Flamengo players surrounded Colombian referee Oscar Ruiz to protest at his performance. One, midfielder Nelio, pushed the official in the back.
Others appeared ready to join in when about 20 riot police, with plastic shields, moved in to escort him off the pitch while the Chileans celebrated.
Shortly before the final whistle, a brawl in the Colo Colo penalty area held up play for five minutes and ended with Colo Colo midfielder Fabian Guevara being sent off.
Seconds before, Jose Luis Sierra of Colo Colo and Fabio Baiano, a Flamengo substitue, were dismissed for fighting.
Colo Colo played the last 10 minutes with defender Pedro Reyes in goal after their first-choice goalkeeper, and his replacement, were both injured.
But the Chileans won with a spectacular goal by Marcelo Espina in the 86th minute. They took the quarter-final tie 2-1 on aggregate and meet Cruzeiro of Brazil in the semifinals.
